rule: A provider's docs requirements table must list exactly the packages declared as dependencies in that provider's pyproject.toml — no more, no less.
trigger: diff adds a row to a Requirements table in providers/*/docs/index.rst whose package is absent from the provider's pyproject.toml dependencies
rationale: Stale or phantom entries in the requirements table mislead users about what the provider actually needs to install.

evidence.excerpt: pyproject.toml does not declare attrs; please remove from the table

rule: Every provider hook that declares a custom conn_type must have a matching hooks: section and connection-types: entry in provider.yaml so the hook is discoverable in docs and UI.
trigger: diff adds a Hook class with conn_type = "<custom>" but provider.yaml lacks a hooks: block or connection-types: entry for that type
rationale: Without the hooks/connection-types entry the hook is invisible to the Airflow UI connection form and to automated doc generation, unlike all other providers.

evidence.excerpt: Please add a hooks: section and connection-types: entry so the hook is discoverable

rule: Providers must not re-implement operators that already exist in airflow-core/standard (e.g. EmptyOperator); refer users to the core version instead.
trigger: diff introduces an operator in a provider package whose behaviour duplicates a core/standard operator (e.g. a no-op or passthrough task)
rationale: The core EmptyOperator is scheduler-optimised (acknowledged as noop without routing to an executor); a provider duplicate confuses users and loses that optimisation.

evidence.excerpt: core EmptyOperator is optimized, not routed to executor but acknowledged in Scheduler

rule: Provider code (hooks, listeners, plugins) must not call settings.configure_orm(); ORM initialisation is the responsibility of the scheduler/executor context.
trigger: diff inside providers/ adds a call to settings.configure_orm()
rationale: If execution has reached provider code, ORM is already initialised; calling configure_orm() again from a provider is unexpected and indicates a misunderstanding of the execution context.

evidence.excerpt: if running in executor context you should assume ORM is initialized

rule: Provider unit tests must use the provider-specific conn_type when creating test Connection fixtures, not a generic type such as 'http'.
trigger: diff in providers/*/tests/ creates a Connection with conn_type="http" (or another generic type) for a hook that declares its own conn_type
rationale: Using the correct conn_type reflects real-world configuration and catches any conn-type-specific validation or UI behaviour introduced by the provider.

evidence.excerpt: Using provider-specific conn_type reflects real-world configuration and catches conn-type-specific behavior

rule: All __init__.py files under airflow/providers/ namespace directories must use the legacy pkgutil namespace definition (__path__ = __import__("pkgutil").extend_path(__path__, __name__)), not implicit namespace packages.
trigger: diff adds an __init__.py under providers/ (or airflow/providers/) that is empty or omits the pkgutil.extend_path line
rationale: Implicit namespaces conflict with explicit ones; the pre-commit hooks enforce the legacy pattern so that all provider packages remain discoverable alongside each other.

evidence.excerpt: airflow.providers folders should have legacy namespaces, otherwise other providers will not be discovered

rule: Provider RST documentation must use RestructuredText footnote syntax for footnote references, not plain bracketed numbers such as [1].
trigger: diff in providers/*/docs/*.rst adds a reference of the form [N] that is not a proper RST footnote (.. [N] ...) or citation
rationale: Plain [N] notation is not rendered as a hyperlinked footnote by Sphinx; RST footnote syntax is required for correct HTML output.

evidence.excerpt: This should use RestructuredText's footnote syntax

rule: When a provider hook is fully async, the corresponding operator must implement waiting exclusively through the defer/trigger mechanism; a synchronous blocking polling path must not be added.
trigger: diff on a provider operator whose hook is async adds a non-deferrable polling loop (while True / time.sleep) gated by a deferrable=False parameter
rationale: Blocking inside a worker slot wastes resources; Airflow's trigger mechanism exists precisely to avoid holding a worker while polling. Adding a blocking path is considered bad practice.

evidence.excerpt: Polling should be handled by triggers; blocking means you block a worker slot doing nothing

rule: Operators within a provider package must use the parameter name wait_for_completion (not wait_for_termination) to control whether the operator waits for an async operation to finish.
trigger: diff adds a boolean parameter named wait_for_termination to an operator class inside providers/
rationale: Consistent naming across operators in the same package lowers the learning curve for users; wait_for_completion is the established convention in Airflow provider operators.

evidence.excerpt: use wait_for_completion for consistency; easier for users if operators follow the same naming convention

rule: Adding deferrable mode to a provider operator requires both an RST docs update for that operator and a newsfragment file at providers/<pkg>/newsfragments/<pr>.feature.rst.
trigger: diff adds self.defer(...) to a provider operator but providers/<pkg>/newsfragments/ contains no <pr>.feature.rst and/or the operator's RST docs page is not updated
rationale: Deferrable mode is a user-visible feature; the changelog fragment and docs page keep the release notes and user-facing documentation accurate.

evidence.excerpt: No newsfragment under providers/microsoft/azure/newsfragments/ — a 63614.feature.rst would be good

rule: Azure blob path segments must be joined with posixpath.join, not os.path.join, because Azure blob names are always forward-slash-separated regardless of OS.
trigger: diff in a provider transfer or hook for Azure Blob Storage uses os.path.join to construct a blob name or path
rationale: os.path.join uses backslash on Windows, producing invalid blob names; posixpath.join is unambiguous and cross-platform.

evidence.excerpt: Azure blob names are always /-separated, but os.path.join uses \ on Windows

rule: Use str.removeprefix() instead of str.replace(prefix, "", 1) when stripping a known leading prefix from blob or file path strings.
trigger: diff uses .replace(some_prefix, "", 1) to strip a leading path prefix from a string
rationale: str.replace finds the first occurrence anywhere in the string, not just at the start, so it can incorrectly strip a mid-string occurrence; removeprefix is unambiguous.

evidence.excerpt: str.replace finds the first occurrence anywhere, not just at the leading edge; removeprefix is unambiguous

rule: Airflow triggers must yield a TriggerEvent with a timeout status and descriptive message when a polling timeout is reached, rather than breaking out of the loop without yielding.
trigger: diff in providers/*/triggers/*.py contains a polling loop that reaches a timeout condition and uses break (or return) without yielding a TriggerEvent
rationale: Breaking silently leaves the operator with no event to act on; the operator never learns the real reason for termination, masking timeouts as errors or hangs.

evidence.excerpt: Why not yield the timeout TriggerEvent immediately instead of break?

rule: In trigger timeout paths, cancellation side-effects must be wrapped in their own try/except so the timeout TriggerEvent is always yielded with the correct reason, not the cancellation error.
trigger: diff in providers/*/triggers/*.py performs a cancel call inside a timeout branch without an independent try/except around that cancel call
rationale: A transient failure on the cancel call must not replace the timeout message with a cancellation error message; the user must always see the real reason (timeout) for trigger termination.

evidence.excerpt: cancel fails, falls through to outer except, yielding cancel error instead of 'Timeout waiting…'

rule: Provider plugin class docstrings must accurately describe only the events that are actually registered and handled by that plugin.
trigger: diff adds or modifies a docstring on an AirflowPlugin subclass that claims to handle event types (e.g. DAG run events) not implemented in the plugin body
rationale: Overpromising in user-facing plugin docstrings misleads users who rely on docs to understand plugin behaviour without reading source code.

evidence.excerpt: plugin only registers a task-instance listener; docstring claims DAG run events too
